I understand the frustration — you've done everything right, and we've confirmed your line is in good shape on my end: Active, roaming-enabled, with 2 GB of refueled data available and full 5G/4-bar signal. So the remaining causes are all device or configuration settings. There are a few known culprits for MMS specifically, even when data is working fine:

**1. APN / MMSC settings (most common cause)**
MMS relies on a specific server address (the MMSC URL) stored in your APN settings. If it's missing or incorrect, picture messages fail while everything else works — which is exactly your symptom.
- Go to **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network → Access Point Names (APN)**
- Check whether an MMSC URL is present
- If it's blank or looks wrong, use **Reset to default** (the menu option in the top-right of the APN screen)
- **Then reboot your device** — the reset won't take effect until you restart

**2. Messaging app permissions**
The messaging app needs Storage and SMS permissions to attach and send photos.
- Go to **Settings → Apps → Messages (or your messaging app) → Permissions**
- Make sure **Storage** (or Photos and videos) and **SMS** are both set to **Allow**

**3. Wi-Fi Calling interference**
In some cases Wi-Fi Calling conflicts with MMS. Worth checking since your Wi-Fi was off earlier:
- Go to **Settings → Network & internet → Wi-Fi Calling**
- If it's **ON**, turn it **OFF** and then test a picture message

Could you check those three and let me know what you find — particularly whether the MMSC URL is present in your APN settings? If the APN reset and permissions check out and it's still failing, tell me and we'll go from there.
